links.outcome: Clinician workflow satisfaction, burnout, and documentation time comparing two ambient scribe products in randomized crossover pilot
links.effect: Product B yielded greater satisfaction improvement (2.51 vs 1.91; mean difference 0.60, 95% CI 0.32-0.90) and greater reduction in minutes-in-notes (B - A = -3.19 minutes; 95% CI -4.87 to -1.50) than product A.
links.quote: Clinicians reported greater improvements in satisfaction with product B (2.51 points on a 7-point scale) compared to product A (1.91 points; mean difference: 0.60, 95% CI: 0.32-0.90).

links.outcome: Local assessment of ambient scribe usability, clinician well-being, and time savings
links.effect: Both tools reduced personal and work burnout and improved workflow satisfaction; product B reduced minutes-in-notes more (-3.19 min); no meaningful differences in pajama time or patient-related burnout.
links.quote: Both tools reduced personal and work burnout scores, but differences between tools were not meaningful.

screen.reason: This is a randomized crossover trial evaluating the real-world deployment of two ambient AI scribe technologies among outpatient clinicians, measuring burnout, satisfaction, and documentation time.
